resvg.notes: renderer of record for the optimisation loop

chromium.notes: SVG is wrapped in HTML with body{background:#000} and svg{width/height=size}; the SVG root is its own stacking context

headline_recommendations: Stack glow layers with style="mix-blend-mode:screen" (CSS style= or a <style> class, NOT the presentation attribute). Byte-identical in both engines at every stack depth measured (N=1..16: max diff 0 LSB), and equal to sRGB-space 1-(1-a)(1-b).

Never use mix-blend-mode:plus-lighter: chromium implements it (exact additive), resvg silently ignores it (renders as normal). Measured divergence on a 10-layer stack: rms 3.73 LSB, max 109 LSB, core pixel 194 vs 255.

Always give every filter an explicit filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x/y/width/height. With the default region (-10%,-10%,120%,120% of the GEOMETRY bbox) resvg DROPS the element completely for a large blur on a thin shape while chromium clips it; and a perfectly horizontal or vertical straight segment (zero-height/zero-width bbox) vanishes in BOTH engines.

Always write color-interpolation-filters explicitly (sRGB or linearRGB). The SVG default is linearRGB and both engines honour that, but the invalid/auto value diverges (resvg->linearRGB, chromium->sRGB). For additive glow that matches sRGB screen math use sRGB.
Margin of 3*stdDeviation around the filtered geometry is enough for zero clipping in both engines at sigma 40 (measured: 2.75*sigma already 0 LSB loss at full 255 amplitude; 2.5*sigma loses 1 LSB).

Effective sigma differs: resvg ~0.98x nominal, chromium ~0.94x nominal, i.e. resvg blurs 3.5-5.3% wider. Tune stdDeviation on the renderer of record and expect the other engine's glow to be ~4% tighter/looser.

Prefer radialGradient/linearGradient-filled shapes over feGaussianBlur for the broad bloom: both engines agree to <=1 LSB (rms 0.33) and resvg renders a full-canvas radial gradient in ~195 ms vs ~105 ms PER blurred layer.

resvg filter cost scales with filter-region AREA: 10 identical sigma-24 layers took 2963 ms over a 1184x1184 region vs 757 ms over a 320x910 region. A 40-layer blur stack costs resvg 4.1 s vs chromium 0.53 s.

1_feGaussianBlur.method: white bar/line on black, filterUnits=userSpaceOnUse region >= 3*sigma margin, color-interpolation-filters=sRGB; horizontal profile averaged over 200-264 rows to beat 8-bit quantisation; models fitted by least squares (scipy)
1_feGaussianBlur.evidence: profiles are EXACTLY zero beyond ~2.82*sigma (a true gaussian would still be 2.4e-3 of peak at 2.82 sigma); the 3-box step response fits chromium with rms 0.22-0.27 LSB vs 0.62-0.65 for an erf

effective_sigma_summary.definition: sigma_eff = sqrt(variance of the fitted 3-box kernel) = sqrt(3*(d^2-1)/12)

1_feGaussianBlur.small_sigma_warning: at sigma 2 the two engines disagree by 19% on the peak of a 1px line (51 vs 43) and by 8% on a 6px line (227 vs 210); at sigma 5 the sign flips (resvg 19/111 vs chromium 21/121). Blurs with sigma <= ~5 are NOT portable at the few-LSB level.

blurred_dot_engine_agreement.note: 16x16 white square blurred, max abs diff over whole canvas

2_filter_region.zero_area_bbox_kills_the_element_in_both: a path 'M 300 500 L 700 500' with stroke-width 40 and a default-region filter renders NOTHING in either engine (zero-height bbox -> zero-height region)

default_region_with_sigma40_on_a_thin_li.chromium: clipped to the 1.2px/8px-wide region, peak correct (15 for a 6px line)

resvg_narrow_region_bailout.note: userSpaceOnUse region, 6px white line, sigma 40; resvg renders nothing until the region is ~26px wide

minimum_margin_for_sigma40.recommendation: margin = 3*sigma (both engines exactly 0 LSB loss); absolute kernel support is 1.5*d = 2.82*sigma chromium / 2.96*sigma resvg

objectBoundingBox_padding_needed_for_a_6.pad_0.1_default: 5.8% of the stroke ink lost (outer 6.8px of each side cut) in BOTH engines

2_filter_region.explicit_regions_agree: userSpaceOnUse and objectBoundingBox explicit regions produce identical rectangles in both engines to within 1px of outward rounding (resvg 241px vs chromium 242px wide on one sub-pixel case)

mix-blend-mode_as_presentation_ATTRIBUTE.note: must be inside style="" or a <style> rule

style_mix-blend-mode_lighten.correction: an earlier degenerate probe (equal layer values) made this look unsupported; with base 96 / top 48 both engines return 96

plain_alpha_over.agreement: POOR in deep stacks: resvg rounds, chromium truncates; N=16 layers of 8% white -> 186 vs 182 (ideal 187.8)

feComponentTransfer_linear_gamma_table_d.agreement: exact on all four types tested

3_compositing.colour_space_of_element_blending: sRGB (non-linear) in both engines: 3 screened layers of grey 64 give 148, matching 255*(1-(1-64/255)^3)=147.8, not the linear-light 106.7

cif_missing_default.conclusion: BOTH engines default to linearRGB inside filters

isolation.blend_reaches_the_parent_stacking_contex: a screen-blended child sees everything painted below it in the same stacking context (probe 112 over a 64 backdrop)
isolation.isolating_ancestors_measured: filter, mask, clip-path, opacity<1 and isolation:isolate on the parent group ALL cut the backdrop off (probe drops 112 -> 64) - identical in both engines
isolation.group_level_blend: a group with mix-blend-mode:screen and normal children does not add its children together; the children composite normally inside the group, then the whole group screens onto the backdrop (measured 64/64/64 inside, 112 over the backdrop)
isolation.inside_a_mask: mask content is an isolated group in both engines; mix-blend-mode:screen between two mask shapes works and gives the same 64/112 as on the canvas

plain_alpha_vs_screen_ink_divergence.note: 10 identical sigma-30 blurred layers over rgb(1,2,7)

3_compositing.identical_layer_banding_warning: N identical layers quantise to N-LSB steps (10 identical layers produced only G values 2,12,22,32). Use distinct sigmas/opacities per layer, or fewer brighter layers.

blend_mode_sweep_base96_top48.method: opaque grey-96 backdrop, grey-48 rect on top with style=mix-blend-mode:<mode>, probe at the overlap
blend_mode_sweep_base96_top48.conclusion: every separable CSS blend mode tested is supported and identical in both engines; plus-lighter is the ONLY divergence (resvg falls back to normal)

color-interpolation=linearRGB_on_the_mas.verdict: AVOID setting color-interpolation on a mask

4_masks_and_gradients.gradient_in_a_mask: linearGradient white->black in a mask, applied to a white bar: engine profiles agree to <=1.5 LSB (row-averaged samples 255/212/170/127/85/42/0 in both)
4_masks_and_gradients.maskUnits_maskContentUnits: maskUnits=userSpaceOnUse and maskContentUnits=objectBoundingBox both work in both engines; obb content gradient samples agree within 1 LSB (240/127/16 vs 239/127/15)
4_masks_and_gradients.stroke_opacity_times_mask: multiplicative and identical: stroke-opacity 0.5 under a 0.5-luminance mask gives 64 in both engines (unmasked 128)
4_masks_and_gradients.gradient_on_a_stroke: stroke="url(#lg)" works in both; gradientUnits=userSpaceOnUse and objectBoundingBox give identical values (obb maps to the GEOMETRY bbox, stroke excluded); peaks along the arc 18/73/128/182/237 (resvg) vs 19/74/128/183/237 (chromium)

gradient_color-interpolation_DIVERGES.verdict: never set it; the sRGB default agrees to <=1 LSB

4_masks_and_gradients.radialGradient_verdict: radialGradient (incl. gradientTransform, fx/fy focal point and the SVG2 fr attribute) agrees between engines to max 1 LSB / rms 0.33-0.38 over the whole canvas, and is ~15x cheaper than a blur layer in resvg

5_colour_and_gamma.key_finding: For a MONOCHROME shape on transparency, color-interpolation-filters has NO measurable effect in either engine: sRGB, linearRGB and the default gave byte-identical blurred profiles (peak 59/15, fwhm 24/98). Only alpha is being convolved, and alpha is linear in both spaces.

two_colour_blur_junction.note: white bar abutting a grey-64 bar, sigma 10, value at the junction pixel

additive_combination_inside_a_filter.note: three grey-64 copies summed with feComposite arithmetic

5_colour_and_gamma.recommendation: Put color-interpolation-filters="sRGB" on every filter. It costs nothing for the blur shape itself, it makes any in-filter combination match the sRGB screen math used for the element-level stack, and it removes the auto/invalid-value divergence.

6_antialiasing_and_hairlines.sub_pixel_strokes_are_linear: coverage integral (sum/255 across a near-vertical cut) equals stroke-width: 0.25 -> 0.25/0.24, 0.5 -> 0.49/0.48, 1 -> 0.93-1.00, 2 -> 2.00/1.99, 3.2 -> 3.25/3.19, 6 -> 6.00/5.99 (resvg/chromium). Neither engine clamps to a minimum hairline.
6_antialiasing_and_hairlines.centre_line_agreement: sub-pixel stroke centroids agree between engines to 0.08-0.19 px (0.13 px at y=400, 0.08-0.19 px at y=650)
6_antialiasing_and_hairlines.apex_scanline_artifact: on the single scanline through an arc's x-extremum both engines lose 7.5% of the coverage (row sum 236 instead of 255; neighbouring rows are correct). It disappears at 4x supersampling. Do not model this 1-row dip.
6_antialiasing_and_hairlines.1024_vs_4x_supersampled: the direct 1024 render differs from a 4096 render box-downsampled 4:1 by rms 0.7 LSB (resvg) / 0.7-1.3 LSB (chromium), max 55-108 LSB on individual edge pixels

shape_rendering.crispEdges: AA OFF in BOTH engines (peak 255, width snapped to whole pixels, centre snapped to 464.0); 3.2px stroke becomes exactly 3px
shape_rendering.verdict: never set shape-rendering; engines then disagree by up to 255 LSB on edge pixels

7_avoid_list.why: resvg ignores it entirely; chromium implements it. 10-layer stack: core 194 (resvg) vs 255 (chromium), rms 3.73 LSB
ignored by BOTH engines - silently no blending. Use style="..." or a <style> class

7_avoid_list.construct: default filter region with a large blur
7_avoid_list.why: resvg drops the element (0 ink), chromium clips it

7_avoid_list.construct: filter on a perfectly straight horizontal/vertical segment without an explicit region
7_avoid_list.why: zero-area bbox -> element disappears in BOTH engines
resvg falls back to linearRGB, chromium to sRGB: 109 vs 192 on the same additive chain
chromium switches the luminance calculation (128 -> 55), resvg ignores it
chromium honours it (64/128/191 -> 137/187/224), resvg ignores it
turns AA off in both engines and quantises geometry; per-pixel differences up to 255 LSB
resvg rounds, chromium truncates; 16 layers -> 4 LSB divergence, and 28% total-ink divergence in the faint halo of a 10-layer blurred stack
per-layer 8-bit quantisation produces N-LSB banding (10 identical layers gave only the G values 2,12,22,32)
resvg drops the element, chromium renders it unfiltered - a silent, very visible divergence while iterating
spec says the element must not render; both engines instead render it unfiltered (consistent, but not spec, so don't rely on it)

baseline_ms.note: chromium's 231 ms is process startup; subtract it for per-frame cost

engine_diff_vs_stack_depth.note: the ~4% sigma difference accumulates: a 40-layer blur stack differs by rms 1.1 LSB / max 18 LSB between engines

9_integration_test.note: 10-layer two-arc glow stack (sigma 0..60) over rgb(1,2,7). screen: rms 0.79, max 40, identical core pixel (212,241,241). plain alpha: rms 2.33, ink ratio 1.20. plus-lighter: rms 3.73, max 109. single big filter with an arithmetic chain: rms 0.98, max 65.
9_integration_test.background_is_preserved_exactly: rgb(1,2,7) reads back as (1,2,7) in both engines - a flat dark background needs no special handling
